detail: A small feed-forward neural network (e.g. 2-3 hidden layers with dropout) could capture non-linear feature interactions beyond what Gradient Boosting finds, particularly spatial interactions between latitude/longitude and income.
Apply SHAP values to the Gradient Boosting/Random Forest models to explain individual predictions (e.g. 'why was this specific block group priced at $350k'), important for underwriting transparency.
Extend beyond the 1990-census-era California Housing dataset to current multi-state parcel-level data with school ratings, crime statistics, and walkability scores.
Run Bayesian optimization (e.g. Optuna) over Gradient Boosting's learning rate, depth, and number of estimators, rather than the default settings used in this baseline research pass.

direction: Real-time prediction / deployment as a web API
detail: Wrap the best model in a lightweight Flask/FastAPI service accepting block-group features and returning a live price estimate, with model versioning for periodic retraining as housing prices drift over time.

Test spatial cross-validation (holding out entire geographic regions) instead of random splits, since random splits can leak neighbouring block groups between train and test and overstate generalization.

Examine whether the model systematically under/over-predicts values in historically under-invested areas, since price data can encode historical inequities that a naive model would learn to reproduce.
